title: Noble's Backgrounds in "What's Opera, Doc?"
content: One of the greatest classic short cartoons is"What's Opera, Doc?"a 1957 Warner Brothers Merrie Melodie directed by Chuck Jones.The story features Elmer Fudd as the demi-god Siegfried chasing Bugs Bunny and singing "Kill the Wabbit!" In less than seven minutes, they manage to satirize Wagner, expressionist cinema, ballet, and Fantasia, all at once.Maurice Nobel did the layouts and backgrounds, and they add immense scale, color, and drama to the piece.Noble said: "Starting rough and not getting specific too early will allow you to keep your design ideas flexible…The more ideas and work you have, the more design possibilities you will have to choose from.""I suggest putting all your research materials away once you start designing and never refer to them again. This may prove difficult at first. But I’ve found that if you are tied too closely to your reference, your designs will tend to look stiff. You will miss out on many fun design opportunities."----MOREWatch "What's Opera, Doc?" on Archive.orgArt book on Maurice Noble:The Noble Approach: Maurice Noble and the Zen of Animation DesignQuotes fromCartoon Brew.All images ©Warner Bros.
